text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Spike in 5xx/timeouts on /v1/generate (p99 latency) — synthetic monitor threshold breached. Current affected region: eu-west-1.
Alex K: saw the alert, deploy finished ~3m ago from canary -> stable. p95 jumped to ~1.8s, p99 to 6.2s and 502/504s climbing.
Maria P: Confirming prod dashboard — 5xx rate ~10% over last 5m, gateway timeouts and model-worker errors. Error signature: "kvcache-miss -> OOM?" in a few logs.
Samira R: Any recent infra flags? I pushed a small batching optimization earlier today but only to canary. That shouldn't hit stable.
Alex K: I saw the same release had a minor kernel change in runtime-libs. Canary looked fine earlier though. Rolling back stable now to v2027-11-rolling-789.
Derek L: oncall here, taking lead for mitigation. @Alex K if you rollback, please include the exact kube command and let me know when done.
Alex K: executing rollback:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/redwood-api redwood-api=redwood/redwood-api:v2027-11-rolling-789 --record
kubectl rollout status deploy/redwood-api -n inference
```
Alex K: started rollout (rs/rollout 0->1).
IncidentBot: Deploy bot: Rollout started by Alex K for redwood-api -> v2027-11-rolling-789.
Maria P: While rollback is in progress, I'm toggling short-term gateway timeout increase to reduce 504 noise (from 10s -> 18s) and activating our fallback route to cached-models.
Jordan T: tagging support — customer X (enterprise-astoria) reported timeouts on live inference; CS has been notified to set expectation.
Samira R: I'm tailing logs from model-workers to check for OOM patterns:
```text
[worker-3] ERROR: kvcache handle failed: alloc 256MB failed, attempted 2 retries
[worker-7] WARN: slowed token generation, waiting on KV-sync
```
Derek L: Looks like memory pressure spikes correlate with the time of the new kernel change. Do we have a quick config to reduce per-request batch size?
Alex K: pushing a conservative env override to runtime: `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024 -> 768` on canary only; not touching stable yet (rollback first).
oncall-sre: Rollout status: 50% pods updated -> 1m. Health checks are passing on new replicas.
Alex K: rollback completed, new pods at rev v2027-11-rolling-789. Observability note: p95 dropped to 750ms, p99 trending down to 1.2s. 5xx rate back to baseline (~0.3%).
Maria P: Gateway timeout bump reverted to 10s now. Fallback route disabled.
Derek L: Good. Can we validate synthetic checks and a few customer flows? @Samira R can you run the internal smoke suite and non-blocking load test?
Samira R: running smoke + 5m flood test (50 rps) against eu-west-1. Results: 0.2% 5xx, p99 1.3s for the endpoint, no OOMs in logs.
Jordan T: CS confirms customer X reports resumed normal operation. They're asking what happened — will draft a brief customer-facing note.
Alex K: Root cause hypothesis: kernel-level change in runtime-libs increased peak memory usage in certain request shapes -> KV cache pressure -> stalls -> gateway timeouts. We'll open a follow-up postmortem and attach traces.
Derek L: Action items: 1) Mark this incident as mitigated. 2) Create follow-up to revert the runtime change from the release branch and add a memory regression test. 3) Notify customers and update status page.
IncidentBot: Incident mitigated by rollback at 1799991268. Severity: SEV2 (customer impact, degraded p99) — follow-up required.
Alex K: I'll create the PR to revert the kernel change and add a canary with memory-pressure test.
Maria P: I'll coordinate the customer note and postmortem draft.
Derek L: Handing off to oncall-sre for postmortem tracking. If anything re-emerges, page me.
oncall-sre: acknowledged, tracking CI:INC-1799991111. Closing thread after postmortem created.
